result.killer: No single killer. Things that weaken it: the free official guide and annexe template on myasbl.lu, a guide for medium ASBLs due in autumn 2026, ASBLs left out of the LBR sanctions phase with no date set, free filing help from the Agence du bénévolat, and filing by PDF upload. The ministry's templates timing (QP 64616) is unverifiable because the PDF text could not be extracted.
result.reason: Nothing kills it outright. I found no Luxembourg-specific ASBL accounting or filing tool. Generic tools (My Member Software, AssoConnect, Odoo) and business tools such as Sage BOB do not show a Luxembourg fit. But the case is weak. The state gives free help: myasbl.lu has the small-association accounting guide in FR/EN/DE and an official "annexe aux comptes ASBL" template, and a guide for medium ASBLs is due in autumn 2026. Filing is a PDF/A upload, so a tool can't automate much. Paperjam says ASBLs are outside the LBR sanctions phase that started 21 September, with no date set for sanctions. The Agence du bénévolat helps small groups with filing for free. Buyers are volunteer treasurers with little money. I couldn't read the ministry's QP 64616 reply on templates.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: CNS direct immediate payment (PID) is the main billing channel. About 49-57% of doctors and dentists use it, and traditional reimbursement was due to end on 1 Jan 2026 (the CNS says so; a July 2025 press piece says PID is still voluntary, unresolved). The medical convention expires on 31 Oct 2026 and the AMMD refuses the new one. State-run PID platform, no clear software gap. No PID or e-health duty found for labs or physiotherapists.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pseudoephedrine medicines became prescription-only from 1 Dec 2024 (Ministry of Health). No new narcotics-register law found. Legal base is the 1973 law and the 1974 grand-ducal regulation. Pharmacies are few and well served by existing software. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security (gardiennage) needs authorisation from the Minister of Justice, plus ministerial approval of each agent. Bill 8031 (amending the law of 12 Nov 2002) is late-stage: Council of State second complementary opinion 9 Jun 2026, committee report 2 Jul 2026. It adds event security, rules on guard dogs, fines of EUR 500-50,000 and a ban on agency temps and sub-contracted self-employed guards. One secondary source gives 1 Nov 2026 as the date (unconfirmed). Cleaning: no specific rule found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: On-site register of workers (Labour Code L.211-29, kept 5 years), ITM safety notice, health and safety coordination plan, posting declarations via free e-Détachement. SNSFP merged into ITM on 1 Jan 2025. No 2025 law creating a new register. Posting side is covered by K01 and K04.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Real estate agents and developers are supervised by the AED (law of 12 Nov 2004, extended in 2020). AED circular 792 of 26 Jan 2026 covers client identification. TCSP and domiciliation providers must register with AED, and SPF annual certification is due by 31 Jul. The co-ownership law of 1975 is being reformed (video general meetings, April 2025). Mostly handled by fiduciaries and compliance vendors.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Guest registration form (fiche d'hébergement): law of 28 Feb 2025 in force 1 Sep 2025, now fully digital through the free Lux Héberge app and MyGuichet, for every guest aged 15+. No sanction for late filing. No national tourist tax found. Short-term rentals: commune declaration, and an establishment authorisation above 89 days a year.

coverage.category: 32. ASBL and foundation accounting and RCS/RBE compliance (country-specific)
coverage.found: Law of 7 Aug 2023: three ASBL size classes. Small ones (under 3 FTE, income up to EUR 50,000, assets up to EUR 100,000) file a cash statement plus a simplified annex. Grand-ducal regulation of 17 Feb 2025 sets the annex. Transition ended 23 Sep 2025. Accounts due within 6 months of year-end, filed within a month of approval. LBR sanctions phase from 21 Sep 2026 under the law of 23 Jan 2025 (ASBL excluded for now). Free official guide at myasbl.public.lu.

coverage.category: 33. Short-term rental / furnished let operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: Commune declaration, establishment authorisation above 89 days a year, 89-day cap in residential zone 1, EU short-term-rental registration regulation. About 1,100 dwellings in short-term use (Jan 2026 parliamentary answer). Mostly private landlords. No new filing duty found.

coverage.category: 34. Construction and demolition waste (country-specific)
coverage.found: Waste law of 21 Mar 2012; bill 8482 amends it (status unknown). Building materials inventory required on demolition (Art. 26). Chambre des Métiers is asking for an exemption for small jobs. No register obligation for artisans confirmed.

coverage.category: 35. Tobacco, alcohol and cabaret licences (country-specific)
coverage.found: Customs (Douanes et Accises) grants tobacco and cabaretage authorisations under the 1989 cabaret law. Spot checks in 2025 found shops without a licence. Budget law 2025 set a minimum excise on new tobacco products. No periodic filing duty for small shops confirmed.

coverage.category: 36. Property managers (syndics) and co-ownership (country-specific)
coverage.found: The 1975 co-ownership law is being reformed (April 2025 ministerial answer; remote general meetings). The Groupement des syndics professionnels is in the working group. Syndic AML status unconfirmed. No bill text found.

coverage.found: AED registration and AML supervision of domiciliation; SPF annual certification due 31 Jul; AED circular 792 of 26 Jan 2026. Served by fiduciaries and established compliance vendors.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Public supply is run by communes and 6 water syndicates (SEBES, DEA, SEC, SES, SIDERE, SESE). The Law of 23 Dec 2022 (Mémorial A704, in force 1 Jan 2023, transposes Directive 2020/2184) sets risk-based duties. Dates: catchment-zone risk analysis by 12 Jul 2027; supply-system risk analysis by 12 Jan 2029. The state tool LuxWSP and the Drëpsi label (AGE audit) already cover supplier risk assessment, so no private software gap there. The law also covers 'installations privées de distribution' (owner's responsibility) and 'lieux prioritaires' (large places open to the public, to be listed by grand-ducal regulation). The list and the exact owner duties are unverified. Luxembourg Direction de la santé recommends hot-water 55-60C and keeping a network plan and maintenance protocol (circular 3729). I found no Luxembourg-specific hotel or campsite Legionella testing or logbook rule. Candidate C1 below. Small private operators of their own supply were not found beyond the 10 m3/day or 50-person exemption, which does not apply to commercial or public activity (this comes from the 2002 text; I did not confirm the 2022 thresholds).

Dates: 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium firms; 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small firms (a search summary says timber micro and small firms, already under the EUTR, are on the earlier date; unverified). Wood traders already have EUTR records; the LCB (Le Commerce du Bois) offers a collective due-diligence system. The EU TRACES NT system handles organic import certificates (e-COI) and first-consignee duties. Bill 8156 would set the ALVA official-controls framework for third-country products (status unverified). Luxembourg is landlocked, so fish catch certificates are not relevant. Only generic EU-wide EUDR vendors seen (osapiens, Greenly, eudr.co). No Luxembourg-specific operator count found. Candidates C2-C3 below.

result.competitor: I found no Luxembourg ASBL-specific accounting or filing software. Luxembourg accounting tools target businesses and fiduciaries (Sage BOB, WinBooks, Horus, Orbis Finance, Caseware Lux FinTax, PwC e-Accounts, KPMG). Free state help: the guide comptable de la petite association on myasbl.lu, the good-practices guide, the LBR helpdesk and the Agence du bénévolat. A parliamentary reply cited the ministry's plan for accounting templates for small and medium ASBLs; I could not extract the PDF text to confirm this, so their timing is unverified. Because filing is a PDF upload, a third-party tool cannot automate submission much. French and German association SaaS was not checked for Luxembourg fit (not_reached).
result.duty: Law of 7 Aug 2023 (Luxembourg, in force): every ASBL keeps accounts. A small ASBL (at most 3 FTE, revenue at most EUR 50k, assets at most EUR 100k) prepares a receipts-and-expenses statement plus an annex; the annex form is set by a grand-ducal regulation of 17 Feb 2025. Larger ASBLs use double entry. The general assembly approves the accounts within 6 months of year end and they are filed with the RCS within the following month (guichet: within 7 months), electronically at lbr.lu with LuxTrust or eID. Annual. Possible sanctions: legal actions inadmissible, dissolution, penal (art. 71). Per Paperjam (9 Oct 2026), ASBLs are outside the coercive phase launched 21 Sep 2026; LBR can only measure compliance from 2026 accounts filed in 2027. A parliamentary document says ASBLs file in classic format (no eCDF) and the standard chart of accounts (PCN) does not apply to them.
result.market: 8,612 ASBLs registered at 30 June 2026 (LBR via Paperjam). Between 16 Dec 2025 and 16 Jun 2026 there were 5,138 ASBL filing requests, of which 1,403 were annual accounts. Most ASBLs are likely small cash-basis volunteer bodies; the share able to pay is unknown.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under Luxembourg's law of 7 August 2023, every ASBL must keep accounts sized to its activity (small ones: a receipts-and-expenses statement plus a standard annex) and file them yearly at lbr.lu within about 7 months of year end. Possible sanctions are administrative or judicial dissolution and penal penalties (art. 71), but none have been applied to ASBLs yet; checks start with 2026 accounts filed in 2027. I found no Luxembourg ASBL-specific tool, only business software (Sage BOB, Orbis, Caseware) and fiduciaries. Against it: the free state accounting guide covers the small-ASBL job, the ministry plans free templates, filing is a simple PDF upload, the work is yearly, volunteer treasurers pay little, and the market is about 8,600.

The duty is real: guichet.public.lu describes MENJE agrement, a mandatory education-and-care contract, a 12-child cap, and CSA provider recognition with an annual activity report. The market is tiny and shrinking. A parliamentary document, probably from about 2022, gives 448 active assistants and says the number keeps falling, so I could not verify a current count. They are home-based sole carers with little spend. CSA reform (MENJE press kit, Jan 2026) and bill 8686 are in flux, which adds uncertainty. I did not read whether the state CSA portal already handles billing, and I found no dedicated software. The niche is too small to support a business. I ran only 2 searches and opened no pages, so the competition check is incomplete.

Duty is real: law of 23 Jan 2025, LBR sanctions phase began 21 Sep 2026 (registered letter at T, warning T+30d, extract notes T+60d, EUR 40/day capped at EUR 3,600 after 7 months, strike-off at 12 months). Paperjam counts about 53,337 dossiers in scope, mostly missing annual accounts (38,716), missing national ID numbers and address mismatches. Weaknesses: it is a one-off remediation wave rather than recurring, and defects are fixed once. The LBR portal shows defects to filers, and fiduciaries, PwC and law firms offer remediation. Luxgap sells RBE vs RCS cross-checking. Buyers are fragmented and the fix is a small filing task. Not a good fit for a standalone SaaS. Competitor search was shallow, and no direct micro-company monitor was found.

The duty is real. Law of 12 Nov 2002 requires ministerial authorisation (5 years, renewable), per-agent approval with an honorability check, and prior approval of service-rule changes. Bill 8031 was adopted 7 Jul 2026 (law of 17 Jul 2026 per frontaliers-grandest). It takes effect 1 Nov 2026: no agency temps or self-employed guards, and a 25-150 EUR fee per approval request. Event-security access rules apply from 1 Feb 2027. No named competitor found, but I did not check generic tools. The firm count was not found, and the market looks tiny, probably a few dozen firms. Most duties are one-off approvals, not a recurring workflow, and large firms probably dominate. I could not verify the fines of 500-50,000 EUR. Low buyer volume, so the score is 3.

Law of 23 Dec 2022 is real. Government timeline lists risk analyses in "réseaux domestiques" by 12.01.2029, so a duty is planned. I could not find the grand-ducal regulation listing lieux prioritaires, or the owner duties (sampling, registers, penalties), or site counts. The 2019 Santé circular on Legionella is recommendations only (sports halls, schools, campsites), not binding. No Luxembourg logbook software found. Only Novalair (service) and foreign vendors. The deadline is over 2 years away, the duty is unclear, buyers are scattered and the market is small, so urgency and willingness to pay are weak. The duty is likely to fall mostly on communes and large buildings, not small firms.
